Mutiny

MYOO-tih-nee -- stress on the first syllable, MYOO. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Mutiny is an open rebellion against those in authority, especially by soldiers or sailors.

Facing spoiled rations and brutal discipline, the sailors plotted a mutiny against the captain.

Worked Example

Halfway across the ocean, the crew seizes the armory, locks the officers in their quarters, and votes to sail the ship home.

An organized uprising by a crew against its own commanders is a mutiny. Unlike a complaint or a protest, a mutiny is open rebellion -- the group rises up to defy and displace the authority set over it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rebellion: open resistance to authority or control

revolt: an uprising against those in power

insurrection: a violent rising against a government

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

obedience: willing compliance with orders

allegiance: loyalty and devotion to a leader or cause

Where it sits · how serious the rising becomes — revolt → mutiny → insurrection

revolt vs. mutiny: Revolt is broader and can be smaller in scale than mutiny -- any group can revolt against any authority, while a mutiny is a pointed uprising by people bound to obey, such as a crew turning on its own captain.

insurrection vs. mutiny: Insurrection goes further than mutiny: a mutiny overthrows the leaders of one ship, unit, or organization, while an insurrection is a violent rising aimed at a government itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mut-

root — mut-: to move, to rise up (Old French meute 'revolt,' from Latin movere 'to move')

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: state, condition, or activity of (French -ie)

Put it together

Put it together: Mutiny traces through Old French meute, 'a revolt or movement,' back to Latin movere, 'to move.' At the root, a mutiny is a mass movement -- a whole crew or company rising up and setting itself in motion against its own commanders.

Use the root in a new word: commotion

Use the root in a new word: commotion: A sudden commotion in the hallway turned out to be two escaped hamsters from the science lab.

Root Check

Word Choice

Mutiny classically belongs to ships and armies -- crews mutiny against captains, soldiers against commanders -- but it extends to any organized group openly defying its own leadership: 'the staff was on the verge of mutiny.' It is far stronger than grumbling or dissent; mutiny means open rebellion.
